title: Error Handling and Configuration Knowledge Check
description: Check your understanding of Node.js error handling, async failures, Express error boundaries, environment configuration, safe logging, and graceful shutdown.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: Why should required configuration be validated at startup?

options.text: To fail early with a clear error instead of running with invalid settings

questions.explanation: Startup validation catches missing or malformed config before the app starts serving traffic.

questions.prompt: What should an Express error handler usually produce?

options.text: A consistent HTTP error response and safe logging

questions.explanation: Centralized error handling standardizes status codes, response shapes, and logging behavior.

questions.prompt: Which data should generally not be included in production error logs?

options.text: Secrets such as tokens, passwords, and API keys

questions.explanation: Logs are often widely accessible, so secrets and sensitive personal data should be redacted.

questions.prompt: What is graceful shutdown meant to do?

options.text: Stop accepting new work, finish or drain active work, and close resources

questions.explanation: Graceful shutdown reduces dropped requests and resource leaks during deploys or restarts.
